# omada_gateway_ip_mac_binding (Resource)

Manages one entry of the gateway's IP-MAC binding table (Device Config > Gateway > IP-MAC Binding in the controller UI). The gateway keeps a static ARP entry for each bound pair, so it can still reach a client whose dynamic ARP entry has expired, for example a sleeping host woken by a directed wake-on-LAN packet. Targets the Open API v1 surface (`/openapi/v1/.../sites/{siteId}/ip-mac-binds`). The controller addresses an entry by its binding id; the import id is `<site_id>/<mac>` and Read resolves the id. This resource never reads or changes the site-wide ARP spoofing defense setting, so it can't restrict the gateway to bound clients only. Requires one of: `Site Settings Manager Modify` or `Network Config Page Modify`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Site ID that owns the binding. Provide it via a variable or data source so the
# value is not hard-coded in checked-in configurations.
variable "site_id" {
  type = string
}

# The LAN network the bound address belongs to.
resource "omada_lan_network" "office" {
  site_id        = var.site_id
  name           = "Office"
  vlan_id        = 110
  gateway_subnet = "192.168.110.1/24"
  interface_ids  = [] # gateway LAN port ids

  dhcp_settings = {
    enable       = true
    ipaddr_start = "192.168.110.100"
    ipaddr_end   = "192.168.110.254"
  }
}

# Hand the desk PC a fixed address...
resource "omada_dhcp_reservation" "desk_pc" {
  site_id = var.site_id
  mac     = "00-00-5E-00-53-19"
  ip      = "192.168.110.19"
  net_id  = omada_lan_network.office.network_id
}

# ...and bind the pair on the gateway, so the gateway keeps a static ARP entry
# for it. A directed wake-on-LAN packet from the gateway then still reaches the
# PC after it has slept long enough for its dynamic ARP entry to expire.
resource "omada_gateway_ip_mac_binding" "desk_pc" {
  site_id      = var.site_id
  mac          = omada_dhcp_reservation.desk_pc.mac
  ip           = omada_dhcp_reservation.desk_pc.ip
  interface_id = omada_lan_network.office.network_id
  description  = "desk PC (wake path)"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `interface_id` (String) ID of the interface: the `network_id` of an `omada_lan_network` when `interface_type` is `lan`, or a WAN port ID when it is `wan`.
- `ip` (String) IP address bound to the MAC. It must lie in the subnet of the interface.
- `mac` (String) Client MAC address, format `AA-BB-CC-11-22-33`. Case and separators (`-`, `:`, `.`, none) are ignored when matching the controller's entry. Changing it updates the entry in place.
- `site_id` (String) Site ID the binding belongs to. Changing this forces replacement.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Optional description, 1 to 64 characters. Do not store secrets here.
- `export_to_dhcp_reservation` (Boolean) Whether the controller also exports the pair to the DHCP reservation table ("Auto-export to DHCP reservation" in the UI). Defaults to false. The exported reservation is not managed by this resource; manage reservations with `omada_dhcp_reservation` instead.
- `interface_type` (String) Type of the gateway interface the binding applies to: `lan` (a LAN network) or `wan` (a WAN port). Defaults to `lan`.
- `status` (Boolean) Whether the binding is enabled. Defaults to true.

### Read-Only

- `binding_id` (String) Binding ID assigned by the controller.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# An IP-MAC binding is imported as <site_id>/<mac>.
terraform import omada_gateway_ip_mac_binding.desk_pc 64b000000000000000000001/00-00-5E-00-53-19
```
